- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ values if sentiment volatility > 0.5.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was positive recently — if so, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If true outcome is significantly above forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was negative recently — if so, increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits recent volatility — use 15-day moving average as a smoothing anchor.
